name: Teachers, Prophets and Reformers of the World's Faiths
description: From Mahavira and the Buddha to the Reformation and the leaders of today, the religious figures who founded, renewed or reshaped great traditions.

checkpoints.name: The age of teachers
checkpoints.note: In India and China, Mahavira, the Buddha and Confucius teach ways of living that shape huge parts of Asia. Their dates are traditional, and their words were written down by followers.

checkpoints.name: New faiths spread
checkpoints.note: Jesus's teaching is carried round the Mediterranean by Paul, and Muhammad founds a community in Arabia. Ali's leadership leads to the lasting split between Sunni and Shia Muslims.

checkpoints.name: Mystics, monks and masters
checkpoints.note: Kūkai, Shankara, Hildegard, Francis, Rumi and Nichiren teach in monasteries and on the road, each giving their tradition a new voice in Japan, India, Germany, Italy and Persia.

checkpoints.name: The Great Reformers
checkpoints.note: Guru Nanak founds Sikhism, and Luther's challenge to Rome in 1517 begins the Reformation. Zwingli and Calvin build new churches, while Ignatius and Teresa renew the Catholic one.

checkpoints.name: Faith in the modern world
checkpoints.note: Wesley, Joseph Smith, Mother Teresa, the Dalai Lama, two popes and Desmond Tutu show religion at work in preaching, new movements, charity, exile and the fight against apartheid.
